'Six' is stale from before the EntityJoinLevelEvent helper-sweep was added.

problems.quote: Overpacked's `GiantBackpack.hurt` drops the entire backpack as an item and discards the entity
problems.issue: Not on a hit. In overpacked-2.0.1 `GiantBackpack.hurt` does `SetDamage(get_damage() + amount * 10.0f)` and only takes the drop-and-discard branch when the source `isCreativePlayer()` OR the accumulated damage exceeds 40.0f — i.e. roughly five bare-hand punches, not one. The drop itself is additionally gated on the `doEntityDrops` gamerule (`spawnAtLocation` is skipped without it, but the entity is still discarded). The same simplification is repeated in the limits table row "Someone hits the helper entity".
problems.correction: "Overpacked's `GiantBackpack.hurt` accumulates damage (`amount × 10`) and, once that passes 40 — or on a hit from a creative player — spawns `get_stack()` as an item (only with `doEntityDrops`) and discards the entity."

problems.issue: The 'Slots' column gives the container sizes, not what the player sees. `GiantBackpack.CreateInventory` allocates 55/28/28, but `GiantBackpackMenu` sets `rows = inv_id == 0 ? 6 : 3` and adds only `rows * 9` ShulkerBoxSlots — 54 for the centre, 27 for each side. The 55th slot of the centre container is the sleeping-bag slot (`SetSleepingBag`/`get_sleeping_bag` use `inv[0].getContainerSize() - 1`), which the backpack GUI never shows. The later sentence about `CreateInventory` building "all three containers (55/28/28)" is correct because it names the containers.
problems.correction: Either label the column "Container" or give the visible numbers: 54 / 27 / 27 (centre container 55 incl. the hidden sleeping-bag slot).

problems.quote: Overpacked 1.x has no such concept; there every compartment always exists.
problems.issue: Cannot be checked from this repository: only `libs/overpacked-2.0.1-1.21.1-neoforge.jar` is vendored, there is no 1.x jar anywhere, and no test note records a 1.x run. problems.quote: Switching the module off at runtime makes the handler return at once and leaves Overpacked's own modifier in place, because the `NORMAL`-priority handler writes it again on the next tick.
problems.issue: The page's sentence is correct with Overpacked installed, but it points at a genuine gap in the Java (SlowdownFeature.java:40-42): when the module is switched off at runtime the handler returns before touching the attribute and never removes the modifier it last wrote. On a pack WITHOUT Overpacked nothing rewrites it, so our last `overpacked:speed` value sticks until relog (harmless at the 0.0 default, but a real residual slowdown if `slowdown_multiplier > 0` and something carried a `CUSTOM_DATA` `Count`). Efficiency note from the same method: `data.copyTag()` is called twice per stack per tick per player, deep-copying the whole backpack NBT — double what Overpacked itself does.
problems.correction: No page change required. In the Java, remove the `overpacked:speed` modifier once on the disabled path, and read `copyTag()` into a local.
